clue.text: Releasing pressure, drain the boil

indicators.note: releasing pressure means letting the pressure letter out of the word before it

parts.note: to drain is to seep away
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Advice for a pressure cooker: let off steam, drain off the boiling water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Releasing pressure' reads as advice about a boiling pan, but it tells you to let P out of the word for drain.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to bubble violently, the way liquid does when it boils.

clue.text: Stop when one gets in hot water?

indicators.note: one getting in means the letter for one is placed inside the word for stop

parts.note: to stem a flow is to stop it
A is one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A riddle about when someone finds themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot water' usually means trouble; here it is literal, vapour off boiling water, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour rising from boiling liquid is water heated past its boiling point.

clue.text: Sovereign loses head in rage over soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the next one
losing its head means the word for rage drops its first letter

parts.note: a temper is a fit of rage
OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A ruler, furious, has lost his head in front of his troops.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMPER loses its head, T, to give EMPER; OR (Other Ranks) goes below it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme monarch ruling an empire.

clue.text: I charm no snakes with a mouth organ

indicators.note: to snake is to wind about, so the letters twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A snake charmer confesses he uses a mouth organ, not snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snakes' looks like the object of 'charm' but is the anagram signal; 'with' joins the A on.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a small wind instrument played with the lips, also called a mouth organ.

clue.text: Tender athlete's foot with a bit of wretched fungus

parts.note: tender in the sense of gentle or mild

indicators.note: the foot of a word is its final letter
a bit of a word here is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Treating athlete's foot, that wretched fungal infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like a verb (to treat) but is the adjective MILD; 'athlete's foot' gives E, the last letter of 'athlete'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildew is a whitish growth caused by a mould on plants and damp surfaces.

clue.text: Sunless mediterranean island with an air of coldness

indicators.note: sunless means the island's name loses S, the abbreviation for sun

parts.note: Sicily is the largest island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean island without sunshine would feel cold.
explanation.walkthrough: S is a standard abbreviation for sun; take it off SICILY.
explanation.definitionFit: To act icily is to behave in a frosty, unfriendly manner.

clue.text: More than one study about on-target earnings indicates…

indicators.note: about means the plural for studies wraps round the earnings abbreviation

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room, so DENS is more than one
OTE is the recruitment abbreviation for on-target earnings

explanation.surface: Research into sales pay packages shows something, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into 7-down's surface; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote something is to signify or point it out.

clue.text: … at what point women have it hard — and with what

parts.note: where asks at what point or place
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a report on when women face difficulty, and how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' and 'and' are link words; the definition is the final 'with what'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherewith is an old-fashioned word meaning by which means or using which.

clue.text: Gives personal nursing service

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so the answer lies within the words Gives personal

explanation.surface: Someone offers individual care as a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing' suggests caring for the sick but signals letters held in giVES PERSonal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening church service of prayer.

clue.text: I reopen redeveloped institute

indicators.note: redeveloped means the letters are reworked into a different shape

explanation.surface: Someone reopens a college building after renovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Institute' looks like a noun but is the verb, to set up or found.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer something is to found or set it up for the first time.

clue.text: Jackson overcame hurdles to get it

definitions.text: Jackson overcame hurdles to get it

parts.words: Jackson overcame hurdles to get it
parts.note: Colin Jackson, a Welsh hurdler, cleared the hurdles for the top prize: read literally, not as overcoming difficulties

explanation.surface: Someone named Jackson beat the obstacles to win something.
explanation.walkthrough: Colin Jackson was a British sprint hurdler and world champion; 'overcame hurdles' is literal track athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: The top award at a championship or Olympics, given for first place, is made of the precious yellow metal.

clue.text: Research that shows early signs of development

definitions.text: Research that shows early signs of development

parts.words: Research that shows early signs of development
parts.note: reads like economics or business, but the early development is that of an unborn creature

explanation.surface: A study reveals the first hints of economic growth.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of biology studies the formation of organisms before birth or hatching.

clue.text: One has several branches in street

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the word street

explanation.surface: A chain shop with many outlets on a high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' suggests a business; it is boughs.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak or elm grows boughs out from its trunk.

clue.text: Firm grip, without pressure, agitated dog

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: agitated means the remaining letters are stirred into a new order
without means the pressure letter is removed from grip

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A firm hold, no force, on a nervous dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' reads as describing the dog but signals the rearranging of what is left of 'grip' once P goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed, famously kept by the British royal family.

clue.text: Evil archer almost shot knight

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken up, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word archer loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A wicked bowman nearly shot a mounted knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ARCHER to ARCHE; 'shot' rearranges EVIL plus ARCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalier is a French title for a knight or cavalier.

clue.text: Household words?

definitions.meaning: relating to the home, as in chores or appliances
a row between partners, angry words exchanged at home

explanation.surface: A question about common phrases.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a 'domestic' is a quarrel at home, a sense the police use; the question mark flags that unusual meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this means a family argument; as an adjective it means relating to the home.

clue.text: Is monkey initially sustaining swinging movement?

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up the one above it

parts.note: swinging, as in the Swinging Sixties, means fashionable and modern

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of monkey

explanation.surface: A question about whether a monkey's swinging supports itself.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the later pieces sit beneath the first, holding it up: that is 'sustaining'. 'Swinging' recalls the Swinging Sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: Modernism was an early twentieth-century artistic trend breaking with tradition.

clue.text: A voter's upset with new energy reform

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A disgruntled voter demands fresh vigour in political reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the voter's mood but signals the rearranging of A VOTER with N.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate is to restore or overhaul, giving something a fresh form.

clue.text: Work extra large amount for one living in Australia

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation for extra large
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: Someone works overtime for a big payout while living Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: Australia has possums, a marsupial family related to the American one; the setter treats the names as interchangeable.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsupial of this family is found in the Americas, with related possums in Australia.

clue.text: Change of heart in death shows extent of wisdom

indicators.note: changing the heart means the middle letter of death is swapped for another

explanation.surface: Facing death changes one's mind and shows how wise one is.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of DEATH is its middle letter A; changing it for P gives the answer. The clue does not name the new letter, so the definition must confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth here means profundity, how far wisdom or knowledge goes.

clue.text: Foolishly oppose adopting one Indian baby

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the jumble holds the letter for one
foolishly means the letters of oppose are jumbled

parts.note: A means one, a single thing

explanation.surface: A protester unwisely objects to taking in a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' rearranges OPPOSE; 'adopting' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A papoose is a Native American infant, or the sling for carrying one.

clue.text: Cereal initially supplies one with energy

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of supplies

parts.note: A means one, a single thing
go is energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Breakfast food gives you energy to start the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like it belongs to 'Cereal'; it applies to 'supplies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith used in puddings, classed as a cereal food.

clue.text: One out of four children develops plaque with start of decay — true? Almost!

indicators.note: develops means the letters change into a new form
the start of decay is its first letter
almost means the word true is missing its final letter

explanation.surface: A dental question: a child's plaque leads to decay, is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: PLAQUE, D (start of decay) and TRU (true almost) are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Quadruplets are four children born together, so one of them is a single member of the set.

clue.text: Trick question leads to irritation, resentment and kerfuffle

indicators.note: leads means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tricky query causes annoyance, bitterness and fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trick question' reads as one phrase; 'Trick' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A quirk or trick is a peculiar habit or mannerism.

clue.text: Run scored by minor player

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run added to the total not off the bat, such as a wide
a film actor with a tiny non-speaking part

explanation.surface: A substitute scores a run.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs from byes, wides and no-balls rather than hit by a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean an addition: a bonus run in cricket and a background performer in a film.

clue.text: Flatter fleece material

parts.note: to oil someone is to flatter them, smooth them over
to fleece is to skin, to swindle someone

explanation.surface: Smooth talk to swindle someone out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a comparative adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilskin is cloth treated with oil to make it waterproof.

clue.text: Cook to stir round dish

indicators.note: cook means fiddle with, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: cook, stir and serve the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges TO STIR into RISOTT, then O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice meal cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Religious education to produce convert

parts.note: RE is the British school abbreviation for religious education
to make is to produce

explanation.surface: Religious lessons that aim to win new believers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convert' suggests a religious convert but is the verb, to transform.
explanation.definitionFit: To remake something is to change it into a different form.

clue.text: After a short time, return to live a simple form of life

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a brief time

indicators.note: return means the word for living is read backwards

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: After a brief pause, life comes back in its simplest form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is only a link word here, not an order signal; the pieces run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, among the most basic living things.
